Winters get cold here so I have been looking into building a greenhouse, basically making my patio into an attached greenhouse. But it has limited space so I wouldn't be able to grow much if I planted in the dirt or by container gardening. A few years ago I became interested in hydroponic gardening but "regular" hydroponic systems keep everything on one flat(ish) plane so that wouldn't increase my available growing area. Yes, hydroponic yields are greater than dirt gardening but my patio is still too small.

Then I saw a video about wall gardens which would increase my available growing space, but it's best used for lettuces, swiss chard, basil ... you know, plants that are not too heavy and don't take up lots of room. Pros: wall gardens can be made with common materials found in home stores, you water at the top and it flows down by gravity, and it's attractive if you creatively arrange the plants in a pattern. Cons: it takes up your wall space and you can't plant (too much) in front of it so as to block the sunlight, and it needs to be perfectly level vertically so the water flows down to each plant below where you water.

Then I thought a tiered hydroponic system would be best but access to plants on the far end would be limited. A workaround for that is to make the hydroponic troughs removable, like commercial systems, so that an entire trough could be removed and all the plants accessed in that way. It's easy to make it yourself (a fraction of what you'd pay to buy such a setup) and would greatly increase the number of plants I could put in that 1.5 sq m area (about 5 feet by 5 feet usable space on that side of the patio). I can go up about 2m (6 or 7 feet) or so. With careful planning and knowing the height of each plant I calculated I could grow about 30 plants versus 10 to 15 in the dirt or in pots. So the tiered system at least doubles the yield, and since it's inside a greenhouse enclosure I can start planting in late February instead of early May extending the growing season and increasing overall yields yet again.
